:::: pm-about
# About me {.unnumbered .unlisted}

I am a veterinarian and a One Health epidemiologist. I earned my Master of Public Health (MPH) in One Health from the University of Arizona as a Fulbright Scholar. My research looks at infectious disease epidemiology, surveillance, and ways to improve disease prevention and control.

I am currently a Pre-PhD Research Fellow with Worldwide Veterinary Service (WVS), hosted at the Malawi–Liverpool–Wellcome Research Programme. My research explores why canine rabies continues in southern Malawi despite repeated mass dog vaccination, using integrated vaccination, surveillance, dog movement, and human exposure data to inform elimination strategies. My broader research experience spans zoonotic and neglected tropical diseases, antimicrobial resistance, and community-based surveillance.

My work brings together field research, epidemiological analysis, and teamwork across human and animal health sectors. I am especially interested in spatial epidemiology, infectious disease modeling, and One Health approaches that support better public health decisions.

**Let's connect and collaborate.** I welcome collaborations in One Health, infectious disease epidemiology and surveillance, particularly work that strengthens health systems in resource-limited settings.
